extracted.intended_audience: independent and self-published authors seeking publicity/press
extracted.subtask_short: indie author PR and press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for indie authors on when to pursue PR, how to write an effective press release, where to pitch, what to avoid, and how to build a long-term publicity strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish PR from marketing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is about newsworthy stories and earned media, not direct 'buy my book' marketing messages. Avoid pitching purely promotional messaging as if it were news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'buy my book' messaging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches that only say 'available now' or 'buy my book' are unlikely to generate coverage. Provide a hook, relevance, or unique angle instead of a plain sales pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch appropriate outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong outlets pitched (NYT for indie genre fiction)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the outlet to the book and audience. Don't mass-blast top-tier outlets uninterested in the genre; prioritize outlets that cover your niche and readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always include a clear hook
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your press release and pitch must tie to news, trend, award, data, or human-interest angle — not just the fact a book exists. The headline should be a hook tied to news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in long-term audience building
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-off PR rarely succeeds long-term. Build direct channels (email list, podcast appearances, collaborations, community engagement) alongside press efforts to convert and retain readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue PR only when there's newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: When PR Works for Authors: award nominations or wins, original data report, hot topic angle, industry recognition, personal story with broader appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PR for demonstrable news/events: awards, proprietary research, topical tie-ins to current events, industry accolades, or personal stories that resonate beyond your immediate circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: news-hooked and specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: hook tied to news, not "Author Releases Book"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a headline that highlights the newsworthiness (award, data, topical tie) rather than a generic release announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: include the 5 W's and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede: 5 W's about the book + author + relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening paragraph should answer who, what, when, where, why and explain why the book matters now or to the outlet's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: provide an excerpt or insight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the body to show what the book offers — an excerpt, key findings (for nonfiction), or a compelling insight that supports the hook and gives reporters usable material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a strong quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote: from author or industry figure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, quotable line from the author or an endorsing industry figure to give journalists ready-to-use text and human context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a boilerplate author bio with credibility markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate: author bio with credibility markers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short author bio listing relevant credentials, achievements, previous awards, or roles that establish authority and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give clear contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a direct contact for follow-up (email, phone, publicist) so journalists can easily arrange interviews or request assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia: book cover, author photo, related visuals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images (cover, author headshot) and any relevant visuals or data graphics; pitches without multimedia are less likely to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target social-first and niche influencers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch visual and short-video influencers specific to book communities when appropriate; they can drive discoverability and sales among reader communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch niche genre podcasts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcasts that focus on your genre or subject are receptive to author interviews and can reach engaged audiences; tailor pitches to each show's format and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target industry-specific media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your book has a professional or trade angle, approach trade publications and industry outlets that cover those audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local/regional press where relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage regional ties or local interest angles to get coverage from hometown or regional outlets that often welcome community-related stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch genre-reviewing bloggers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and contact bloggers who regularly review books in your genre; provide review copies and clear information about the book's themes and readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach niche newsletter writers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many niche newsletters have loyal readerships; craft concise, tailored pitches that explain why your book would interest their subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wire-only distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solely distributing via press release wires without targeted outreach yields low pickup for indie books. Combine wire distribution with targeted pitching to relevant outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass-blasting top-tier outlets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't indiscriminately send the same pitch en masse to top national outlets that rarely cover self-published genre fiction; tailor outreach to appropriate targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't send generic 'available now' pitches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches lacking a hook or news angle are ignored; always lead with relevance or a story rather than availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't omit multimedia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting images or other assets reduces chances of coverage. Always include usable visuals for editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate self-published work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If self-published, highlight what makes the book stand out — awards, unique approach, data, credibility — rather than relying on the publication route alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unverified 'bestseller' claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim bestseller status without verifiable evidence; dishonest claims damage credibility and harm chances with media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and maintain an email newsletter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grow a direct mailing list to control audience relationships and convert press coverage into long-term readers; this complements earned media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue regular podcast appearances
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appear regularly on podcasts to build familiarity with audiences and sustain visibility over time rather than relying on one-off coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with other authors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint promotions, cross-promotion, or anthology appearances can expand reach through peer audiences and lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with genre communities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in online and offline genre communities to build reputation, discoverability, and relationships that can lead to coverage or word-of-mouth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistent content output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular blogging, social posts, or other content keep audiences engaged and provide material to support pitches and press follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an authenticity of author voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch and publicity materials should reflect an authentic author voice rather than contrived PR-speak; authenticity helps stories resonate with editors and readers.
